Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood CSM), Alicia Ng (CTO, Silvermarsh), Marcus Lee (ML Engineer), Priyanka Sharma (Security Lead), Ben Ortiz (Product), Samir Patel (Infra)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: ok hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll wait a minute for folks to get in, but uh to kick off this sync for Silvermarsh, um quick intros?
[00:10] Alicia: yeah hi i'm Alicia, CTO, i'll be the exec sponsor. Marcus is our ml lead, Priyanka handles security.
[00:15] Marcus: Marcus here, thanks.
[00:17] Priyanka: hey all, Priyanka here.
[00:20] Jordan: great thanks. Priya, want to run the agenda?
[00:25] Priya: sure, we'll cover staging and VPC peering, data residency and KMS, pilot scope and acceptance criteria, then operational handoffs - runbooks, credentials, SSO. and then q&a, and next steps. sound good?
[00:40] Ben: yes looks good.
[00:42] Diego: also i'll note we'll follow up with the onboarding playbook as well.
[00:45] Priya: cool. first, staging: our recommendation is set up a small Dedicated-like pool in your dev VPC via private peering, that tends to mimic production performance and lets us run KV cache and batching tests. for folks on this call, is private peering acceptable?
[01:10] Samir: from infra's side peering is fine, we just need the CIDR and egress rules. can you send the exact ports?
[01:20] Priya: yes, i'll paste the runbook - note that some customers call it "Redwood Dedicate" in the notes, transcription sometimes shows that, but it's Redwood Dedicated. ports 443 outbound to api.redwood-inference and specific egress to our monitoring endpoints. i'll include the full list.
[01:40] Samir: ok also we need the firewall team to review NAT behavior, we have strict egress.
[01:45] Jordan: understood. Priya will share a short-runbook with the network snippet.
[01:50] Priya: i'll put that in the follow-up — sample cURLs, IAM role examples, and a small terraform snippet for peering.
[02:05] Alicia: on data residency — we have a hard requirement that any PII-including prompts or evaluation sets for EU patients must not leave EU. we need to know if Hosted supports EU-only region for inference.
[02:25] Jordan: yes Hosted has an EU region; however, for guaranteed residency and audit control we'd recommend Redwood Private or Dedicated in an EU tenant. for Hosted we can restrict region, but the control plane still touches metadata; so depends on regulatory comfort.
[02:45] Priyanka: can you clarify the control plane comment? our compliance team is worried about metadata egress.
[02:52] Jordan: sure, control plane has ops telemetry. with Private you run a customer-managed control plane so nothing leaves your network, with Dedicated we provide tenancy/isolation and stronger contractual guarantees and SOC2 artifacts.
[03:12] Priyanka: ok that's helpful. do you support HSM/KMS integrations for key wrapping?
[03:18] Priya: (Redwood SE) yes, we support customer-managed KMS via KMS proxies and can integrate with common HSM providers as part of a Private deployment. for Hosted we have envelope encryption and BYOK options with KMS.
[03:30] Marcus: on the ML side, we need to test KV cache behavior for long conversational contexts — some of our prompts are 1.5k tokens and we need to measure latency when we use prefix caching vs cold start. can you provide a benchmark plan?
[03:50] Priya: yes our staging run includes a cold-start profile and a hot-KV profile; we'll run both. for long contexts we typically recommend a quantized model variant and an adjusted batching policy. tradeoffs are latency vs token cost.
[04:05] Marcus: staggered batching might be bad for latency-sensitive endpoints; what's the typical SLO you can deliver for 1.5k tokens?
[04:12] Jordan: depends on Dedicated sizing; but example: with a 4-card pool on A100-ish hardware, you can expect median p95 around 400-600ms for streaming-first-token for that payload... now, transcription sometimes mangles numbers so we'll send benchmark sheets.
[04:35] Ben: and on cost — we need a ballpark, as product will sign off only if unit costs are comparable to what we model.
[04:42] Jordan: yes i'll include the Dedicated capacity workbook. it shows token unit cost, amortized GPU cost, and sensitivity to quantization.
[04:50] Priyanka (customer): question on audit logs — retention policy and access? our security needs 7 years of audit trails for model decisions.
[04:58] Diego: we support audit logging, and log retention is configurable for Dedicated and Private. for Hosted we have limited retention tiers but enterprise add-ons allow longer windows. we'll attach SOC2 folders and audit log docs.
[05:15] Priyanka (Redwood): note that for extremely long retention we'd use our secure long-term storage offering — it's part of the enterprise package.
[05:25] Priyanka (customer): great. also does Redwood ingest training/explainability logs or are those separate?
[05:32] Priya: we capture request/response metadata for quality monitoring; training data ingestion is a separate pipeline. we don't automatically pull user PII into training unless you opt in.
[05:45] Alicia: ok that's critical — we will not opt-in, so we need assurances in the contract.
[05:52] Jordan: yes we'll flag contract language and include a data processing addendum.
[06:00] Marcus: pilot scope — we propose two endpoints: 1) chat summarization for clinician notes (batch inference) and 2) triage assistant (low latency). pilot success criteria: throughput at 200 qps for batch window, p95 latency under 800ms for triage. are those achievable?
[06:20] Priya: they are; we'll design the pilot to measure both. for batch throughput we'll test autoscaling profiles and caching. triage will have a tiny pool with aggressive batching disabled and prefix cache.
[06:35] Samir: related - what about model version pinning and rollbacks? we need a safe rollback plan if a new model regressses.
[06:44] Priya: rollout policies are supported — canary, A/B, and automatic fallback to previous model if quality signals drop. we'll include rollback playbooks. note that eval harness is used to detect regressions tied to prompt sets.
[06:59] Ben: would love to see an example of an eval tied to a prompt set.
[07:04] Priya: we'll share a sample harness and a small eval CSV.
[07:12] Jordan: ok, let's cover credentials and SSO. Samir, do you use SAML SSO already?
[07:19] Samir: yes we use Okta.
[07:21] Diego: we support SAML/SCIM for user provisioning; we'll provide SSO setup docs and a short checklist for attribute mapping.
[07:30] Priyanka (customer): last security Q: encryption at rest for model artifacts and reranker state?
[07:36] Priya (Redwood): model artifacts on Dedicated/Private are encrypted at rest; with Private you can also use your own KMS/HSM keys. reranker state (KV cache) can be stored encrypted and optionally evicted on demand.
[07:52] Alicia: sweet. timeline — we want a pilot in January, ideally mid-Jan. feasible?
[07:58] Jordan: yes mid-Jan is feasible; Diego can coordinate.
[08:02] Diego: I'll propose two slots: Jan 10 or Jan 17 for pilot kick-off.
[08:08] Alicia: Jan 17 preferred.
[08:10] Diego: noted.
[08:12] Jordan: ok wrapping up — to recap, Priya will share runbook and sample scripts, Diego will schedule pilot kick-off for Jan 17, Alicia to confirm residency/EU dataset list, Samir to provide VPC/CIDR and firewall contacts, Jordan to send pricing and Dedicated workbook.
[08:30] Marcus: quick off-script, one more latency nuance — if we use prefix-KV aggressively, do you see cold-start spikes for other tenants?
[08:40] Priya: in Dedicated pools you don't see neighbor noise like multi-tenant hosted env; caching and KV are per-tenant. hosted may have more noisy interference. we'll detail this in the runbook.
[08:58] Ben: ok thanks all.
[09:00] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the deck and runbook within 48 hours.
[09:08] Alicia: thanks, bye.
